title: Capacity slices token rollup: hosted API unit-econ workbook
content:
Purpose:
This sheet rolls up token-level COGS across capacity slices (latency tiers / batch profiles) and regions to produce a reconciled per-million-token COGS and margin waterfall for Hosted API. Intended as a lightweight reconciler between infra chargebacks, model family profiles and pricing experiments.

Executive summary (short):
- Using conservative batch adoption (median batch factor 1.7) we estimate base COGS/M (per 1M tokens) ranges by region from $18 (us-west) to $27 (emea) for Llama-2 style mid-sized models; larger decoder families push +30–60%.
- Key levers: prefix caching uptake, sustained batch factor improvements, and routing to quantized variants. Combined opt actions can reduce effective COGS/M by ~22% in medium-to-high-throughput slices.

Methodology & inputs (tab: Input Assumptions):
- Time window: trailing 30d seq length distribution snapshot (used to assign slice weights).
- Capacity slices: latency (<100ms), mid (100–300ms), bulk (>300ms). Each slice has target batch factor and KV cache hit assumptions.
- Cost inputs: GPU amort + infra ops = $/hour per GPU, power/region uplift, network egress buckets.
- Pricing baseline: example price $0.003 per 1k tokens for margin calcs.

Example per-slice CSV (for quick glance):
region,model_family,slice,median_seq,batch_factor,kv_cache_hit,GPU_type,gpu_hour_cost_usd,tokens_per_gpu_hour,cogs_per_million_tokens_usd
us-west,open-compat,latency,64,1.2,0.12,A10G,2.75,15360000,18.0
us-west,open-compat,bulk,256,4.8,0.45,A10G,2.75,61440000,6.5
emea,open-compat,mid,128,2.4,0.18,A10G,3.25,30720000,21.5
apac,open-compat,latency,80,1.1,0.10,A10G,3.55,15360000,23.1

Sensitivity checks (tab: Sensitivity Monte):
- Run quick Monte with +-15% on batch_factor, +-10ppt on cache hit, and region GPU cost +/-10%. Report distribution of COGS/M and p50/p90.
- Example finding: increasing batch factor by +25% in bulk slice yields median COGS/M reduction of ~8% for that slice, but end-to-end impact depends on slice weight (bulk is only 18% of requests today).

Actionable recommendations (tab: Actionable Levers):
- Short-term (0–6 weeks): expose "bulk-preference" routing for customers with opt-in latency tradeoff; implement per-route batch hints in SDK to increase observed batch factor for long-seq workloads.
- Medium-term (6–16 weeks): automate prefix cache retention tuning per-customer to hit target KV hit % for high-reuse workloads.
- Long-term (Q3+): expand model variants catalog with quantized 4-bit versions for compatible families and set cost-aware routing to prefer these variants in non-strict-latency slices.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Reconcile accounting with finance-led infra chargeback sheet (missing GPU amort windows and reserved capacity credits).
- Decide default customer-level routing policy for mixed-latency customers.
- Validate GPU hour cost with procurement (mix of reserved vs spot pricing).

Notes to reviewer: this is a working rollup to help prioritise engineering work and pricing experiments. Use the Per-slice Rollup tab to adjust slice weights, model families and GPU cost inputs.
